# The Frequency of Light

For thirty-one years, Elias March had spoken no more than four hundred words a day. Most days it was fewer: *Come in from the weather. Supper's ready. You'll catch your death.* A voice directed at himself, or the gulls, or the slow green churn of the sea against the tower's base. The lighthouse on Crag Point had belonged to his father before him, and his grandfather before that, a long unbroken line of men who climbed the one hundred and twelve steps each evening to ensure no ship walked into the rocks at night.

He was sixty-eight now. His knees announced themselves with weather changes. He ate tinned stew from a tin he'd owned since 1987 because replacing it
